 HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE NITIN WASUDEO SAMBRE  HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE ANISH DAYAL  ORDER  % 03.09.2025  W.P.(C) 13534/2025 1.

Having heard the counsel for petitioners at length, what can be noticed from the pleadings in the petition is the challenge to the Public Notice dated 31st July 2025 issued under Section 21 of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act 2013 ('Act of 2013'), with respect to the land described in the prayer clause.

L A C ( N W ) / R e - acquisition/2024/NW/3606 dated 31.07.2025 issued u/s 21 of the New Land Acquisition Act 2013 in respect of This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.

The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 08/09/2025 at 21:59:44 the land admeasuring 490 square yards comprised in Khasra no. 54/18/1 situated in the revenue estate of Village Karala, Jain Nagar, Kungpush, Delhi. b.
Pass any further order/s that this Hon'ble Court may deem fit and proper in the facts and circumstances of the present case."

2. It is the case of the petitioner that the Apex Court in the matter of Govt. of NCT of Delhi v. BSK Realtors LLP (2024) 7 SCC 370, has issued directions in paragraph 58 and that the matters was listed as part of Serial No.53 in List D.1 in DDA v. Tejpal & ors. (2024) 7 SCC 433.

4. Counsel for the petitioner claims that, deviating from the scheme as prescribed under the Act of 2013, the Apex Court has fixed a schedule in This is a digitally signed order.

The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 08/09/2025 at 21:59:44 exercise of powers under Article 142 of the Constitution of India, 1950 ('Constitution'), and the schedule should have been adhered to by the respondents.

5. It is claimed that the impugned notice issued under Section 21 of the Act of 2013 is sans the schedule prescribed and, as such, attracts the consequences under Section 24(2) of the Act of 2013 for not completing the acquisition proceedings within schedule.

6. It is the contention of the counsel for petitioner that the schedule, since it is in deviation from the statutory provisions, i.e. Act of 2013 and is fixed in exercise of powers under Article 142 of the Constitution, has a mandatory effect and, as a sequel, the notice under Section 21 of the Act of 2013 stands vitiated.
7.
Issue notice to the respondents.

Mr. Sanjay Kumar Pathak, Standing Counsel for respondent nos.
1 and 2 accepts notice on behalf of LAC/L&B/GNCTD.

8. Issue notice to the remaining respondent, returnable on 22nd September 2025.
9.

As the original land owner has already expired, an intimation about which is already given by the petitioners to the Land Acquisition Collector, we permit the petitioners to place on record additional affidavit along with other documents.
10. We make it clear that no further action pursuant to the notice under Section 21 of the Act of 2013, as against the land of the petitioner, be undertaken till returnable date.
11. The aforesaid injunction order is passed taking in view the prima facie satisfaction by this Court that the schedule as ordered by the Apex This is a digitally signed order.
